answer: Bind each identity to one distinct registered beehive, inspected each epoch by a licensed apiary inspector who checks colony health, queen presence and hive number. One hive anchors one agent: colonies need seasonal feeding, mite treatment and space, and inspectors cap hives per site. An honest keeper tends one hive cheaply, like writing one sonnet; a farm must buy, house and keep alive a thousand colonies, each pigment-marked queen a separate cost, while dead hives fail like a comet with no tail.
